scenes.text: In 1518, hundreds of people *danced until they died* — and nobody could make them stop.
It started with *one woman* in the city of Strasbourg. Within a month, *hundreds* joined her in the streets.
Doctors at the time had a cure: *more dancing.* They hired musicians and built a *stage* to keep it going.
Some danced for *days straight* — until they collapsed from exhaustion, and some reportedly *died* from it.
One theory: a hallucinogenic mold called *ergot* growing on rye bread. The leading theory now: pure *mass hysteria.*
Terrified townsfolk marched the dancers to a shrine for *Saint Vitus* — the same saint they blamed for *cursing them.*
One of history's strangest unsolved cases. Follow for more *lost secrets* of history.
